chunks: They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say: 'Fighting in it is a great sin, but hindering from the path of Allah and disbelief in Him and the Sacred Mosque and expelling its people from it is greater in the sight of Allah, and persecution is greater than killing. And they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion, if they are able. And whoever of you turns back from his faith and dies as a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between fighting in the sacred month and the greater sin of persecution in Islam?
ai.summary: In the context of the Quraysh's inquiry, this verse establishes a hierarchy of sins, elevating the disruption of religious freedom and the expulsion from the Holy Mosque above mere combat in the sacred month. Shia exegetes emphasize that 'fitnah' (persecution or civil strife) is greater than 'qatl' (killing) because it threatens the very foundation of faith, a concept deeply linked to the Ahl al-Bayt's struggles against Umayyad oppression. The verse concludes by warning that apostasy results in the nullification of both worldly and otherworldly deeds, securing eternal residence in Hell.
